question: The Council’s examination of the Commission proposal to end seasonal time changes (COM(2018) 639) has been at a standstill since 2019. Member States requested further analysis, and, consequently, the Commission launched a study on the impact of ending seasonal time changes. It is now ongoing and is expected to be ready by the end of 2026. The European Parliament adopted its position on the matter in 2019.

However, the Council has still not agreed on a position, and no timetable for a decision has been set. The issue is still very topical – many citizens are frustrated that no progress is being made, and this is eroding trust in EU decision-making processes. In light of the above: 1.
When does the Commission believe the study will be ready?
Can the Commission commit to calling on the Council to resume examination of the proposal no later than six months after publication of the study?
What specific steps will the Commission take to advance work towards a common position on the basis of the study?
